summary: José Celestino Mutis Airport (IATA: BSC) serves Bahía Solano, a remote Pacific coastal town in Colombia's biodiverse Chocó Department. Named after the 18th-century Spanish botanist who extensively documented New World flora, this regional airport is the primary gateway for travelers visiting the Pacific coast's rainforest and famous humpback whale watching grounds. The airport connects Bahía Solano to major Colombian cities since no roads link the town to the rest of the country.
faqs:
Q: What airlines fly into José Celestino Mutis Airport?
A: Regional carriers such as SATENA operate scheduled flights, primarily from Medellín and Bogotá, to Bahía Solano. Flight schedules can be limited, so checking current timetables in advance is recommended.

Q: How long is the typical flight from Medellín to Bahía Solano?
A: Flights from Medellín's Olaya Herrera Airport generally take around 45 minutes to one hour, depending on weather conditions over the Chocó region.

Q: Is the airport open at night or only during daylight hours?
A: José Celestino Mutis Airport operates primarily during daylight hours due to its regional nature and the mountainous terrain surrounding Bahía Solano. Most flights arrive and depart in the morning or early afternoon.

Q: Are there ATMs or currency exchange services at the airport?
A: No, the airport is small and does not have ATMs or currency exchange facilities. It is advisable to withdraw cash in Medellín or another major city before traveling to Bahía Solano.
transport_tips: Taxis and motorcycle taxis (mototaxis) are available just outside the terminal and can take you into Bahía Solano town center, which is only a short ride away. Since Bahía Solano has no overland road connections to other Colombian cities, flying is essentially the only practical way to reach the airport. Hotel pickups can sometimes be arranged in advance, especially during the whale-watching season.
local_tip: Pack a light rain jacket even in the drier months—Bahía Solano is one of the wettest places on Earth, with rain possible year-round in the surrounding jungle.
